visuals.title: Where the bleeding comes from
visuals.text: Usually the anterior nasal septum (Little's area); posterior bleeds come from further back via the sphenopalatine artery.

glossary.Nasal cavity: The air space inside the nose behind the nostrils.
glossary.Nasal septum: The wall of cartilage and bone dividing the nose into left and right sides.
glossary.Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia: An inherited condition causing fragile, dilated blood vessels that bleed easily, especially in the nose.
glossary.Liver disease: Damaged liver makes fewer clotting factors, so bleeding is harder to stop.
glossary.Anaemia: A low haemoglobin level, meaning the blood carries less oxygen.
glossary.Airway obstruction: Blockage of the passage air takes to the lungs.
glossary.Resuscitation: Emergency treatment to restore breathing and circulation, such as fluids and blood.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: measures haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.Full blood count: A blood test measuring haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.Topical: Applied directly to the surface where it is needed.
glossary.Nasal spray: A drug delivered as a fine mist into the nose.
glossary.Silver nitrate: A chemical applied on a stick that seals small bleeding vessels.
glossary.Anterior nasal packing: A pack placed in the front of the nose to press on the bleeding point.
glossary.Ligation: Tying off a blood vessel to stop bleeding.
glossary.Recurrence: The problem coming back after it has settled.
glossary.Internal carotid: The branch of the carotid artery that supplies the brain and eyes.
glossary.External carotid: The branch of the carotid artery that supplies the face, scalp and nose.
glossary.Carotid: The main arteries in the neck supplying the head.
glossary.Antiplatelet: A drug such as aspirin or clopidogrel that stops platelets clumping.
glossary.Haemostasis: The body's process of stopping bleeding by clotting.
glossary.Vessel integrity: How strong and intact a blood vessel wall is.
glossary.Proximal: Closer to the origin, here further upstream in the arterial supply.
glossary.Soft part of the nose: The fleshy lower part below the nasal bones, pinched to compress Little's area.
